style_when: the story is regulatory or contractual — a filing, a mandate, a rate notice, a certificate, a purchase order that changed the economics
prompt: Overhead flat-lay photograph of thick, textured freight contract pages and layered rate tables scattered on a dark, plain matte desk surface. Top-down 90-degree view, even diffused daylight. One thick document page is slightly out of alignment to look handled, resting beneath a heavy brass straightedge ruler. Illegibly cropped paper with muted paper tones, sophisticated editorial color palette, sharp focus on the paper texture, generous negative space around the edges.
negative_prompt: text, letters, numbers, wordmarks, signage, UI, UI elements, human, hands, faces, logos, bright neon colors, typography, watermarks
rationale: The article explicitly focuses on the contractual math, rate tables, and the physical act of 're-reading the sheets they signed.' A document flatlay perfectly captures the regulatory and contractual nature of this hidden margin.
subject: misaligned contractual rate pages under a heavy brass ruler
alt_text: Overhead view of misaligned rate contract pages resting under a heavy brass ruler on a dark desk.
caption: The math behind a fuel surcharge sits in plain sight on rate tables, yet buyers rarely review the specific formula levers they signed.
title: Freight-Fuel-Surcharge-Contract-Flatlay
